findings.trigger: Any store-migrate / store-rollback / core-update that changes state schema or store generation, and any post-rollback historical lookup of pre-migration commit associations.
findings.evidence: The plan states that S9 validates the exact old/new (storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema) tuple against the transition intent and current registry state. In frozen candidate25 the substring storeInstance does not occur anywhere in docs/coop/design-corrections/security/security-lifecycle.schemas.v1.json (probe P2). InstallationTransitionIntentV1 is additionalProperties:false with exactly 11 properties and InstallationTransitionJournalV1 with exactly 20; neither carries a store instance id. The S9.2 registry is a NamespaceList of namespace strings, not a store-instance registry. Separately, security-and-lifecycle.md:654-655 says rollback re-selects the retained old store, while the plan says a newly created/restored store instance receives a new storeInstanceId; the package does not say which applies, and the two readings differ in whether pre-migration association rows still join to the active binding after a rollback.
findings.correction: (a) Withdraw or restate the claim that S9 validates a storeInstanceId tuple: record it as a new private lifecycle obligation requiring an explicit reviewed successor of the S9 intent/journal owner, and name it as a dependency of the separately active versioned-carrier/migration task rather than as already supported. (b) State explicitly whether the retained old store re-selected by store-rollback keeps its storeInstanceId or receives a new one, and state the resulting join behaviour for associations written under the same numeric generation before the migration.
findings.notAtRisk: Uniqueness is sound under either reading: the primary key (storeGenerationDigest, namespaceId, executionId) and both unique keys stay collision-free because a re-selected retained store continues its own receipt counter.

findings.trigger: An observer fail-stop that fires after commit admission has won.
findings.evidence: The text specifies a single atomic attempt state arbitrating latch versus commit admission, and also says an observer latching after admission blocks subsequent effects. Executed probe scratch/rustprobe/src/latch.rs: under the literal reading (a tri-state CAS where latch succeeds only from PREPARING) admit_commit succeeds, the later latch returns false and the state stays COMMIT_ADMITTED, so no record of the observer fail-stop exists and nothing in that state blocks subsequent effects. A four-state machine (PREPARING / COMMIT_ADMITTED / LATCHED / ADMITTED_THEN_LATCHED) satisfies both sentences: post_latch_state=3, commit_permitted=false, further_effects_permitted=false. A 200000-round two-thread probe (scratch/rustprobe/src/race.rs) confirms the arbitration itself is sound: exactly one of latch or commit-admission wins per attempt, zero mutual-exclusion violations.
findings.correction: Name the post-admission state explicitly, or name the separately retained observer fail-stop flag, and name which subsequent effects consult it.

observations.evidence: Because storage implements the security-owned staging trait from another crate, CommitStaging and PreparedLedgerCommit must be pub. Probe scratch/rustprobe/neg/n7.rs compiles (rc 0): a host-side adapter drives security seal_under_append_lock to completion with no storage participation, producing a durable SEAL with no evidence-ledger transaction. This is consistent with the package explicit not-a-sandbox caveat and with F36, and is not an authority breach, but the consequence is not stated.
observations.suggestion: State that the SEAL entry point is reachable by every security-dependent crate, that a deliberately unpaired SEAL is exactly the F36 orphan, and confirm that carrier-capacity and witness accounting do not assume one SEAL per commit attempt.

observations.evidence: Probe scratch/rustprobe/neg/n5.rs reproduces E0509: a commit-state type that implements Drop cannot have its fields moved out, so PreparedCommit publish(self) cannot destructure it to hand CommitSession to begin_journal_txn. The working miniature compiles only because PreparedCommit has no Drop and the inner guards carry it.
observations.suggestion: State that best-effort Drop rollback attaches to the inner guards and the ledger transaction, not to PreparedCommit itself (or that its fields are Option or ManuallyDrop).

observations.suggestion: Reword the grammar.rs description to say it checks already-admitted closure identity and version joins.
